title: Gods' Man — Survival, Reproduction, Illusion #Shorts
description:
The psychology underneath Gods' Man is simpler and older than the story on top. Gods' Man is a wordless novel by American artist Lynd Ward published in 1929. In 139 captionless woodblock prints, it tells the Faustian story of an artist who signs away his soul for a magic paintbrush.

The genes do not care about Gods' Man; they care about copies. To Peck, the mysterious stranger represented Satan and the spirit of death. Gods' Man was adapted into a play written by Daniel "Woody" Weber and directed by Aspacia Lindstrom.

scenes.narration: The psychology underneath Gods' Man is simpler and older than the story on top. Gods' Man is a
wordless novel by American artist Lynd Ward published in 1929. In 139 captionless woodblock prints, it tells the
Faustian story of an artist who signs away his soul for a magic paintbrush. Behind Gods' Man sits
an animal brain negotiating with a story it tells itself. Gods' Man was the first American wordless novel,
and is considered a precursor of the graphic novel, whose development it influenced. Ward first encountered the wordless
novel with Frans Masereel's The Sun (1919) while studying art in Germany in 1926. The nihilist does not
deny Gods' Man — he only refuses
